summary: Malicious SVG files abuse the format's embedded JavaScript support to act as redirectors, self-contained phishing pages, or DOM/XSS script abuse, while appearing to be harmless images. Observed samples masquerade as fake voicemail attachments in spear-phishing campaigns and hide target emails (often base64-encoded) and redirect domains inside obfuscated markup. Because mail and web gateways treat SVG as an image, the format is an overlooked delivery and credential-harvesting vector.
